veranderings.voor: 'n Skuifspeld met 'n laag plastiek of verf om kan die lampie donker hou.
veranderings.na: 'n Skuifspeld wat met 'n laag plastiek of verf bedek is, kan die lampie donker hou.
veranderings.rede: The dangling 'om' directly before 'kan' makes the sentence hard to parse; a relative clause with a comma reads naturally and keeps the meaning.

veranderings.na: om genoeg elektrisiteit daardeur te stuur
veranderings.rede: 'genoeg' has no noun, so the learner must guess what is sent; naming 'elektrisiteit' matches the next sentence and adds no content.

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: Hulle gelei baie swakker as metaal en 'n sel stoot te swak
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: This joins two clauses with their own subject and verb ('Hulle gelei', ''n sel stoot'), so AWS 2017 requires a comma before 'en' ('as metaal, en 'n sel stoot'); I did not propose it because the comma falls inside the protected wording. A person may want to update the protected entry to include the comma.
